outline.chapter_title: Motivation and Challenges of Aligning Large Language Models
outline.description: Introduces the need for controlling LM behavior, reviews existing RLHF pipelines, and highlights their limitations.
subtopics: Capabilities of large unsupervised LMs
Why steering and alignment are essential
Overview of human‑feedback alignment (RLHF)
Complexities of reward modeling and reinforcement learning
Desire for a simpler, more stable method

outline.chapter_title: Foundations: Preference Modeling and the RLHF Objective
outline.description: Formalizes the preference data generation process, the Bradley‑Terry/Plackett‑Luce models, and the KL‑constrained reward maximization objective used in RLHF.
subtopics: Supervised fine‑tuning (SFT) as a reference policy
Human preference collection and the latent reward function
Bradley‑Terry model and its mathematical form
Maximum‑likelihood reward modeling (Eq. 2)
KL‑constrained RL objective (Eq. 3) and its role
Reinforcement‑learning algorithms (PPO, REINFORCE) in practice

outline.chapter_title: From Rewards to Policies: The Closed‑Form Optimal Policy
outline.description: Derives the analytical relationship between any reward function and its optimal KL‑constrained policy, providing the key insight for DPO.
subtopics: Derivation of the optimal policy formula (Eq. 4)
Interpretation of the partition function Z(x)
Re‑parameterizing reward in terms of policy (Eq. 5)
Why the partition function cancels in preference ratios

outline.description: Introduces DPO, shows how the preference likelihood can be expressed directly over policies, and presents the final loss function.
subtopics: Substituting the re‑parameterization into Bradley‑Terry
Derivation of the DPO objective (Eq. 7)
Gradient analysis and the importance‑weight term
Comparison with naive probability‑ratio and unlikelihood methods
Algorithmic pipeline (data collection → reference model → DPO training)
Practical tips: initializing π_ref, choosing β, handling missing SFT

outline.description: Provides rigorous justification for DPO, including equivalence classes of reward functions and consistency with the original RLHF objective.
subtopics: Equivalence relation on reward functions
Lemma 1: identical preferences for equivalent rewards
Lemma 2: identical optimal policies for equivalent rewards
Theorem 1: universal representation of reward classes via π/π_ref
Implications for under‑specification and identifiability
Why DPO recovers the exact optimal policy

outline.chapter_title: Why Standard Actor‑Critic Methods Can Fail
outline.description: Analyzes instability sources in PPO‑based RLHF and explains how DPO avoids them.
subtopics: Control‑as‑inference view of KL‑constrained RL
Derivation of the actor‑critic objective (Eq. 10)
Role of the soft‑value (normalization) term
High‑variance gradients and baseline dependence
DPO’s reward re‑parameterization eliminates the baseline

outline.description: Covers practical aspects needed to reproduce DPO experiments.
subtopics: Data formats for preference triples
Tokenizer and model architecture choices
Computing the log‑ratio term efficiently
Batching, gradient clipping, and optimizer settings
Hyper‑parameter selection (β, learning rate, temperature)
Handling large vocabularies and memory considerations

outline.description: Shows how DPO trades off reward and KL‑divergence on a synthetic sentiment task and compares against PPO and baselines.
subtopics: Task definition and synthetic preference creation
Metrics: sentiment classifier reward, sequence‑level KL
Frontier plots and interpretation
Ablation on β and weighting term
Discussion of why DPO dominates PPO even with ground‑truth rewards

outline.description: Presents results on real‑world preference datasets, evaluation with GPT‑4 and human studies, and comparisons with PPO, Preferred‑FT, and Best‑of‑N.
subtopics: Datasets: Reddit TL;DR, Anthropic HH
Reference model preparation (SFT and Preferred‑FT)
Evaluation protocols (win‑rate, temperature sweeps, GPT‑4 prompts)
Quantitative results: win‑rates, robustness to temperature
Human evaluation methodology and correlation analysis
Analysis of out‑of‑distribution generalization (CNN/DailyMail)

outline.description: Summarizes best practices, common pitfalls, and extensions for practitioners.
subtopics: Choosing a reference policy when SFT is unavailable
Setting β for desired conservativeness
Scaling to larger models (up to 6B and beyond)
Integrating DPO with self‑training or synthetic preference generation
Monitoring KL drift and early‑stopping criteria

outline.chapter_title: Limitations, Open Questions, and Future Directions
outline.description: Reflects on the current boundaries of DPO and outlines promising research avenues.
subtopics: Generalization under distribution shift
Potential reward over‑optimization in the DPO regime
Scaling to multi‑turn dialogue and multimodal generation
Combining DPO with explicit reward regularization
Improving automated evaluation prompts

outline.description: Collects all detailed proofs, derivations, and additional experimental settings referenced throughout the textbook.
subtopics: Full derivation of Eq. 4 (optimal policy)
Derivation of Eq. 7 (DPO loss) from Bradley‑Terry
Proofs of Lemma 1, Lemma 2, and Theorem 1
Extensions to Plackett‑Luce rankings
Additional ablation tables and hyper‑parameter grids
